statute_title: Operating Under the Influence of Liquor or Drugs
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
On a public way or in a place where the public has a right of access
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
Or with a BAC of .08 or higher
enhancements: Child under 14 in vehicle (child endangerment enhancement)
Serious bodily injury or death resulting
notes: Massachusetts uses 'OUI' (Operating Under the Influence). Implied consent under § 24(1)(f)(1). First offense eligible for 24D disposition (alternative disposition with treatment). Lookback period is lifetime.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public way
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or with BAC .08+
No prior OUI convictions
notes: Eligible for 24D alternative disposition — probation with alcohol education program. 1-year license suspension (45 days if hardship license granted with IID).

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public way
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
One or more prior OUI convictions
enhancements: Progressive mandatory minimums for each subsequent offense
notes: Second offense: 2-year license suspension. Third: 8-year suspension. Fourth: 10-year suspension. Fifth+: lifetime revocation. Lookback is lifetime.

offense_class: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public way
While under the influence of marijuana, narcotic drugs, depressants, or stimulant substances
Or the vapors of glue
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of drugs and alcohol
notes: No per se drug limit. Prosecution relies on officer observations, field sobriety tests, and Drug Recognition Expert evaluations. Same penalties as alcohol OUI.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
Recklessly or negligently so as to endanger the lives or safety of the public
notes: Common plea-down from OUI. Mandatory minimum jail time even for first offense. License may be suspended.

elements: Defendant was the operator of a motor vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in personal injury or death
Defendant knew or had reason to know of the injury
Defendant failed to stop and make identity known
enhancements: Death of victim (up to 10 years, 1-year mandatory minimum)
notes: Hit-and-run causing death carries a 1-year mandatory minimum. Property damage only is a lesser offense.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Operation caused the death of another person
mandatory_minimum: 1 year (cannot be suspended, furloughed, or paroled)
notes: Mandatory 1-year minimum that cannot be suspended. Motor vehicle homicide by negligent operation (§ 24G(b)) carries up to 5 years with no mandatory minimum. 15-year license revocation.

penalty_max: 5 years (state prison) or 2.5 years (house of correction)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle recklessly or negligently
So as to endanger the lives or safety of the public
Operation caused the death of another person
notes: No mandatory minimum for negligent operation homicide. Distinguished from OUI-related motor vehicle homicide.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public way
Defendant's license or right to operate was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge or notice of the suspension
notes: OUI-related suspension carries a 60-day mandatory minimum. Additional license suspension upon conviction.

statute_title: Failure to Stop for Police Officer
elements: A police officer signaled the defendant to stop
Defendant failed to stop
Defendant attempted to flee or elude the officer
enhancements: Causing injury or death during pursuit
notes: Charged under general reckless operation or specific failure-to-stop provisions. May also be charged under M.G.L. c. 90 § 25.

statute_title: Possession of Class A, B, C, D, or E Substance
offense_class: Misdemeanor (most first offenses); Felony (Class A subsequent)
penalty_max: 2 years (Class A first); 3.5 years (Class A subsequent); 1 year (Class B); 1 year (Class C/D/E)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Substance is classified under M.G.L. c. 94C
Possession was without a valid prescription
enhancements: Possession near a school or park
notes: Massachusetts decriminalized possession of small amounts of marijuana (under 1 oz for adults 21+). Class A includes heroin, Class B includes cocaine, Class C includes prescription opioids, Class D includes marijuana.

offense_class: Civil Violation (under 1 oz 21+); Criminal (under 21 or over limits)
penalty_max: Civil fine (under 1 oz); 6 months (over 1 oz without license)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
Amount exceeded legal personal use limits or defendant was under 21
enhancements: Possession over 1 oz without proper license
Cultivation beyond home-grow limits (12 plants per household)
notes: Massachusetts legalized recreational marijuana for adults 21+ in 2016 (Question 4). Up to 1 oz on person, 10 oz at home. Over limits without license remains criminal.

statute_title: Possession of Class B Substance — Cocaine
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Class B controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Simple possession of cocaine is a misdemeanor. Larger quantities may support trafficking charges under § 32E.

statute_title: Possession of Class B Substance — Methamphetamine
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Class B controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Methamphetamine is relatively uncommon in Massachusetts compared to opioids and cocaine.

penalty_min: 3.5 years (lowest threshold); varies by substance and weight
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally manufactured, distributed, or possessed with intent to distribute
A quantity meeting or exceeding trafficking thresholds
mandatory_minimum: 3.5 years (lowest thresholds, cannot be suspended or paroled)
notes: Trafficking thresholds: cocaine 18g, heroin 18g, fentanyl 10g, marijuana 50 lbs. Mandatory minimums cannot be suspended. Massachusetts reformed drug sentencing in 2018 (Criminal Justice Reform Act).

penalty_max: 10 years (Class A § 32); 10 years (Class B § 32A); 5 years (Class C § 32B); 2 years (Class D § 32C); 1.5 years (Class E § 32D)
elements: Defendant manufactured, distributed, dispensed, or possessed with intent to distribute
A controlled substance
notes: School zone enhancement adds 2.5–15 years consecutive. Distribution to a minor carries enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant manufactured a controlled substance
Without lawful authority
notes: Methamphetamine manufacturing carries enhanced penalties. Lab cleanup costs assessed against defendant.

elements: Defendant sold, possessed, or purchased drug paraphernalia
Knowing or under circumstances where one reasonably should know it would be used with controlled substances
notes: Marijuana-related paraphernalia for personal use by adults 21+ is legal. Paraphernalia for other substances remains criminal.

penalty_max: 10 years (Class A/B); 5 years (Class C); 2 years (Class D); 1.5 years (Class E)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
With intent to manufacture, distribute, or dispense
notes: Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, and other indicators. Same penalties as actual distribution.

elements: Defendant unlawfully killed a human being
With deliberate premeditation and malice aforethought
Or during the commission of a felony punishable by life (felony murder)
Or with extreme atrocity or cruelty
notes: Massachusetts does not have the death penalty (abolished 1984). First-degree murder carries mandatory life without parole. Three theories: premeditation, felony murder, or extreme atrocity/cruelty.

penalty_min: Life with parole eligibility after 15 years
elements: Defendant unlawfully killed a human being
With malice aforethought
Without deliberate premeditation or extreme atrocity/cruelty
mandatory_minimum: Life with parole eligibility after 15 years
notes: Second-degree murder is any murder that does not meet the elements of first-degree. Parole eligibility after 15 years.

elements: Defendant unlawfully killed another person
The killing was intentional but without malice
Typically in the heat of passion upon adequate provocation
notes: Voluntary manslaughter is an intentional killing mitigated by provocation. Distinguished from murder by absence of malice.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through wanton or reckless conduct
Without intent to kill
notes: Wanton or reckless conduct causing death. Massachusetts does not distinguish penalty between voluntary and involuntary manslaughter.

statute_title: Assault and Battery with a Dangerous Weapon
penalty_max: 10 years (state prison) or 2.5 years (house of correction)
elements: Defendant committed an assault and battery upon another person
By means of a dangerous weapon
enhancements: Serious bodily injury (§ 13A(b)(ii), up to 5 years)
notes: A 'dangerous weapon' includes any object used in a manner that could cause serious injury. Shod foot (kicking) can constitute a dangerous weapon.

elements: Defendant committed an assault or an assault and battery upon another person
notes: Simple assault and battery is a misdemeanor. Causing serious bodily injury elevates to a felony.

penalty_max: 5 years (state prison) or 2.5 years (house of correction)
elements: Defendant assaulted another person
By means of a dangerous weapon
enhancements: Victim is a public employee acting in official capacity
notes: Assault (without battery) with a dangerous weapon. Distinguished from assault and battery with a dangerous weapon (§ 15A).

elements: Defendant committed a larceny from the person
By force and violence, or by assault and putting in fear
notes: Unarmed robbery carries a maximum of life in Massachusetts. Armed robbery (§ 17) has the same maximum but different mandatory minimums.

elements: Defendant committed robbery
While being armed with a dangerous weapon
enhancements: Use of a firearm (5-year mandatory minimum consecutive)
notes: If a firearm is used, mandatory minimum 5 years consecutive under habitual criminal provisions. Masked robbery is a separate enhancement.

penalty_max: 10 years (general); Life (if ransom demanded or victim harmed)
elements: Defendant, without lawful authority, forcibly or secretly confined or imprisoned another person
Within the Commonwealth against their will
notes: Kidnapping of a child (§ 26A) and kidnapping for ransom have enhanced penalties. Enticing a child (§ 26C) is a separate offense.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously set fire to or burned
A dwelling house
enhancements: Person was in the dwelling (§ 1, same statute)
notes: Arson of a dwelling house is the most serious arson charge. Arson of other buildings (§ 2) carries up to 10 years.

elements: Defendant assaulted another person with intent to murder
enhancements: Victim was a law enforcement officer
notes: Charged as assault with intent to murder under § 16. Separate from general attempt statute.

elements: Defendant took and carried away property of another
Without consent
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Larceny from a person (felony regardless of value)
notes: Felony threshold is $1,200 in Massachusetts. Larceny from a person is always a felony.

elements: Defendant took and carried away property of another
Value exceeded $1,200
With intent to permanently deprive
notes: Massachusetts uses '$1,200' as the felony threshold for larceny.

elements: Defendant took and carried away property of another
Value was under $1,200
With intent to permanently deprive
notes: Misdemeanor larceny. Third or subsequent conviction is a felony under § 30(3).

elements: Defendant intentionally took possession of merchandise from a retail establishment
Without paying the full purchase price
With intent to deprive the merchant
notes: First offense under $250 is fine only. Concealment of merchandise on premises creates rebuttable presumption of intent.

elements: Defendant broke into and entered a building, ship, or vehicle
In the nighttime
With intent to commit a felony
enhancements: While armed with a dangerous weapon (§ 14)
notes: Nighttime B&E of a dwelling carries up to 20 years. Daytime B&E (§ 18) carries up to 10 years. 'Nighttime' is between 1 hour after sunset and 1 hour before sunrise.

elements: Defendant broke into and entered a dwelling
With intent to commit a felony
notes: Dwelling B&E is the most serious burglary charge. Nighttime entry and being armed enhance penalties.

elements: Defendant stole a motor vehicle
Or received a stolen motor vehicle knowing it to be stolen
notes: Motor vehicle theft has its own statute with higher penalties than general larceny.

elements: Defendant bought, received, or aided in concealing stolen property
Knowing the property was stolen
notes: Same felony threshold as larceny ($1,200). Knowledge of stolen character is an essential element.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously destroyed or damaged property of another
enhancements: Damage to a house of worship
notes: Includes graffiti and property damage. Restitution typically ordered. Third or more under $1,200 offenses become felonies.

elements: Defendant entered or remained upon the property of another
Without right
After having been forbidden to do so
notes: Low-level offense. Trespass with intent to commit a crime may be charged as attempted burglary.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously destroyed or damaged property of another
Value of damage was under $1,200
notes: Misdemeanor property damage. Three or more offenses elevates to felony.

statute_title: Assault and Battery on a Family or Household Member
elements: Defendant committed an assault or assault and battery
Against a family or household member
Family/household member includes spouse, former spouse, person sharing a child, or cohabitant
notes: Second and subsequent DV offense: mandatory 60 days minimum. Strangulation/suffocation is a separate felony (§ 15D).

elements: Defendant committed a battery against a family or household member
Involving physical contact
enhancements: Prior DV convictions (mandatory minimum 60 days for second+)
notes: Massachusetts uses combined assault and battery statute. No separate battery offense.

statute_title: Wanton or Reckless Behavior Creating Risk of Serious Bodily Injury to a Child
penalty_max: 2.5 years (house of correction) or 5 years (state prison)
elements: Defendant engaged in wanton or reckless behavior
That created a substantial risk of serious bodily injury or sexual abuse
To a child under 18
notes: Covers a range of conduct including leaving children in dangerous situations and exposing children to drugs.

statute_title: Assault and Battery on a Child Causing Serious Bodily Injury
elements: Defendant committed an assault and battery
Upon a child under 14
Causing serious bodily injury
notes: Serious bodily injury to a child carries up to 15 years. Death resulting may be charged as murder or manslaughter.

elements: A valid abuse prevention order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant violated a provision of the order
notes: Mandatory arrest for violations. Federal firearms prohibition applies. 209A orders are the primary DV protective orders.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously engaged in a knowing pattern of conduct or series of acts
Directed at a specific person
Which seriously alarmed or annoyed that person
And would cause a reasonable person to suffer substantial emotional distress
enhancements: Violation of a protective order (§ 43(b), up to 10 years)
notes: Stalking in violation of a 209A order carries up to 10 years. Criminal harassment (§ 43A) is a related offense.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously engaged in a knowing pattern of conduct directed at a specific person
Which seriously alarmed that person and would cause a reasonable person to suffer substantial emotional distress
notes: Pattern of conduct requires at least 3 acts. Includes cyberbullying and electronic harassment.

statute_title: Assault and Battery on Person 60 or Older or Disabled Person
penalty_max: 3 years (simple A&B on elder); 10 years (with dangerous weapon on elder)
elements: Defendant committed an assault and battery
Upon a person 60 years of age or older or a disabled person
notes: Enhanced penalties for crimes against elders and disabled persons. Financial exploitation is a separate offense.

penalty_max: 5 years (state prison) or 2.5 years (house of correction)
elements: Defendant carried on person or had under control in a vehicle
A firearm, rifle, shotgun, or other dangerous weapon
Without a valid license
notes: Massachusetts requires a license to carry (LTC) for firearms. Carrying without a license is a felony.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Felon
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had a prior conviction for a violent crime or serious drug offense
mandatory_minimum: 3.5 years (cannot be suspended, paroled, or furloughed)
notes: Mandatory minimum of 3.5 years that cannot be suspended. One of the most serious firearms offenses in Massachusetts.

penalty_max: 5 years (state prison) or 2.5 years (house of correction)
elements: Defendant carried a firearm on person or in a vehicle
Without a valid license to carry
notes: Massachusetts is a shall-issue state following the Bruen decision. Carrying without a license remains a felony.

statute_title: Discharging a Firearm Within 500 Feet of a Building
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
Within 500 feet of a dwelling or other building in use
notes: Local bylaws may impose additional restrictions. Reckless discharge causing injury charged under separate assault statutes.

penalty_max: 5 years (state prison) or 2.5 years (house of correction)
elements: Defendant knowingly used personal identifying information of another
Without authorization
With intent to commit a crime or to obtain money, credit, goods, or services
notes: Includes phishing, social engineering, and traditional identity theft. Restitution ordered.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with property or had control over property by virtue of employment or position
Defendant fraudulently converted the property to personal use
notes: Embezzlement is a form of larceny under Massachusetts law. Same value thresholds apply.

statute_title: Forgery of Deed, Note, or Other Instrument
elements: Defendant falsely made, altered, or counterfeited a written instrument
With intent to injure or defraud
notes: Includes forging checks, promissory notes, and legal documents. Uttering (§ 5) is a separate offense.

elements: Defendant counterfeited currency, coins, or bank notes
With intent to defraud
notes: Federal counterfeiting charges typically apply. State charges may be concurrent.

elements: Defendant issued a check knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Same value thresholds as larceny. Knowledge of insufficient funds at time of issuance required.

elements: Defendant presented a false or fraudulent insurance claim
Or staged a motor vehicle accident
With intent to defraud an insurer
notes: Massachusetts has specific statutes for motor vehicle insurance fraud. General insurance fraud falls under larceny by false pretenses.

elements: Defendant used a credit card or credit card number
Knowing it was stolen, counterfeit, or without authorization
To obtain goods, services, or money
notes: Includes possession of counterfeit credit cards and skimming devices.

elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction
Knowing the property involved was derived from criminal activity
With intent to promote criminal activity or conceal the source
notes: Massachusetts enacted money laundering statute in 2010. Federal charges may also apply.

elements: Defendant obtained property of another by false pretenses
With intent to defraud
The victim relied on the false representation
notes: General fraud charged as larceny by false pretenses. Same value thresholds as other larceny.

elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with another person
By force and against the will of the other person
Or where the victim was incapable of consent
enhancements: Aggravated rape — victim under 16, bodily injury, or use of weapon (§ 22A, up to life)
notes: Massachusetts uses 'rape' rather than 'sexual assault' in its statutes. Aggravated rape carries up to life imprisonment.

elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse or unnatural sexual intercourse with another person
By force and against the will of the other person
notes: Statutory rape of a child under 16 is charged under § 23 (up to life).

statute_title: Open and Gross Lewdness and Lascivious Behavior
offense_class: Felony (open and gross under § 16); Misdemeanor (lewd and lascivious under § 53)
penalty_max: 3 years (open and gross); 6 months (lewd and lascivious)
elements: Defendant exposed genitals or committed a lewd act
In a public place
Openly and with intent to produce alarm or shock
notes: Open and gross lewdness (§ 16) is a felony. Simple indecent exposure is a misdemeanor under disorderly persons.

statute_title: Engaging in Sexual Conduct for a Fee
elements: Defendant engaged in, agreed to engage in, or solicited sexual conduct
In exchange for a fee
notes: Massachusetts does not criminalize the seller if they are a trafficking victim. Buyers (johns) face prosecution regardless.

statute_title: Posing or Exhibiting Child in State of Nudity or Sexual Conduct
penalty_max: 10 years (state prison) or 2.5 years (house of correction)
elements: Defendant employed, used, or allowed a child under 18
To participate in the production of visual material depicting nudity or sexual conduct
notes: Possession of child sexual abuse material (§ 29C) carries up to 5 years. Federal charges typically apply as well.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
penalty_max: 5 years (state prison) or 2.5 years (house of correction)
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update information
notes: Massachusetts Sex Offender Registry Board (SORB) classifies offenders into Levels 1-3. Level 3 information is publicly available.

elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse or unnatural sexual intercourse with a child under 16
enhancements: Force used (§ 22A, aggravated rape of child)
notes: Age of consent in Massachusetts is 16. No close-in-age exception for sexual intercourse. Indecent assault on a child under 14 is a separate offense (§ 13B).

elements: Defendant was a disorderly person in a public place
Engaging in fighting, tumultuous behavior, or creating a hazard
notes: Broad catch-all public order offense. Often charged alongside other offenses or as a plea-down.

elements: A police officer was effecting a lawful arrest
Defendant knowingly prevented or attempted to prevent the officer from effecting the arrest
By using or threatening to use physical force against the officer
notes: Applies to lawful arrests only. Passive resistance generally does not constitute resisting arrest.

statute_title: Intimidation of Witness or Obstruction of Justice
elements: Defendant willfully endeavored to obstruct justice
By intimidating, threatening, or injuring a witness, juror, or court officer
Or by misleading a police officer in the course of a criminal investigation
notes: Broad obstruction statute covering witness intimidation, evidence tampering, and misleading police.

penalty_max: Varies; typically up to 6 months or until compliance
elements: A valid court order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully disobeyed the order
notes: Criminal contempt is punitive. Civil contempt is coercive — defendant can purge by compliance.

elements: Defendant appeared in a public place while intoxicated
Defendant's behavior was disorderly
notes: Massachusetts decriminalized public drunkenness in 1973. Protective custody (not arrest) is the typical response unless disorderly conduct accompanies intoxication.

statute_title: Default on Recognizance — Failure to Appear
elements: Defendant was released on bail or recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court
Defendant willfully failed to appear
notes: Penalty depends on the underlying charge. Bench warrant issued upon default.

elements: Defendant willfully communicated false information to a police officer
Regarding the commission of a crime
notes: Includes filing false reports of crimes that did not occur.

elements: Defendant willfully threatened to commit a crime against another person
notes: Low-level offense. More serious threats may be charged as assault or criminal harassment.

elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath
In a judicial proceeding
Knowing the statement was false
Statement was material
notes: Massachusetts imposes severe penalties for perjury — up to 20 years.

elements: Defendant gave, offered, or promised a benefit to a public official
With intent to influence the official's action
notes: Covers both offering and receiving bribes. State Ethics Commission may also impose civil penalties.

elements: Defendant was lawfully confined or in custody
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape
notes: Includes escape from prison, jail, court custody, and transport.

elements: Defendant overdrove, overloaded, drove when overloaded, overworked, tortured, tormented, deprived of necessary sustenance, cruelly beat, mutilated, or killed an animal
notes: Massachusetts strengthened animal cruelty laws (Desmond's Law). Aggravated cruelty is a felony.

penalty_max: Up to the maximum of the original sentence
elements: Defendant was on probation for a criminal conviction
Defendant violated a condition of probation
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose any sentence available at time of original conviction. Graduated sanctions may apply.

elements: Defendant was on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Massachusetts Parole Board conducts revocation hearings. Violator may serve remainder of original sentence.

elements: Defendant counseled, hired, or otherwise procured a crime to be committed
Defendant was not present at the commission of the crime
notes: An accessory before the fact is punished the same as the principal. Joint venture liability for those present during the crime.

offense_class: Same as the target offense or lesser penalty
penalty_max: Varies; generally up to the maximum of the completed offense
elements: Defendant attempted to commit a crime
Defendant took a substantial step toward its commission
Defendant had specific intent to commit the crime
notes: Massachusetts punishes attempt at the same level as the completed offense unless a specific lesser penalty is provided.

penalty_max: 10 years (felony) or same as target offense; 2.5 years (misdemeanor conspiracy)
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit a crime
An overt act was performed in furtherance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy to commit a felony punishable by life carries up to 20 years. General conspiracy is up to 2.5 years and $2,000.

statute_title: Trafficking of Persons for Sexual Servitude
elements: Defendant knowingly subjected, or attempted to subject, another person to sexual servitude
Through force, fraud, coercion, or threat
notes: Labor trafficking (§ 51) carries similar penalties. Safe harbor for minor victims. Trafficking victims are not prosecuted.

elements: Defendant confined or restrained another person
Without consent and without lawful authority
notes: Lesser included offense of kidnapping. Covers unlawful restraint without the additional elements of kidnapping.

statute_title: Possession of Class A Substance — Opioids/Heroin/Fentanyl
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a Class A controlled substance
Including heroin, fentanyl, or other opioids
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Class A substances include heroin, fentanyl, GHB, and certain other opioids. Massachusetts opioid crisis has led to expanded treatment and diversion programs.
